history.period: Ancient (Puranic legend); current structure Maratha period
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple on the banks of the Kshipra at Ujjain, regarded as the birthplace of Mars (mangala) according to the Matsya Purana, and believed to sit at the centre of the earth, at the intersection of the prime meridian and the Tropic of Cancer - hence its historic importance for astronomical studies with a clear view of the planet. The current structure dates to the Maratha period, with repairs by the Scindia royal dynasty. The temple's goat (not the usual Nandi) faces the Shivalinga. Mahant Rajendra Bharti is the temple's official (per Wikipedia). It is famed for the Bhaat Puja (Ganesh-Gauri, Mangal Kalash, Panchamrut, Dahi-bhat and Nav Graha pujans), performed to remove mangal dosha - adverse Mars placements affecting marriage, relationships and family life; the Mangal Aarti and Tuesday Mangal Bazaar are other draws.

name: Mangalnath Temple
town_description: Ujjain, on the banks of the Kshipra River, is one of the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) of Hinduism and hosts the Simhastha Kumbh Mela every 12 years. It is an ancient centre of astronomy and Shaivism, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and a rich cluster of temples including Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi, and Mangalnath.
